tickets.title: 11th Street e-bike storage and enforcement
tickets.requester: Assembly Member Keith Powers (elected official); resident speaker (unnamed); District Manager (unnamed); Troy (board member)
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored overnight on and around 11th Street, blocking sidewalks and the street, which residents and businesses say has closed storefronts and hurt building rentals. Delivery workers depend on these bikes, and the district office has worked on the issue since February 2024 without a legal parking or corral site. Action: Ask the precinct and the city to pair the planned October 7 enforcement with a workable site for the bikes and written notice in the workers' languages, and set up a follow-up meeting with the district office on the history of the block.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark spots in Seward Park
tickets.requester: Board member (unnamed); Parks committee representative (unnamed); Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center (reported by Parks committee)
tickets.summary: Residents, park users, and the Lower East Side Ecology Center report more drug use and homeless encampments around Seward Park, and some areas are poorly lit. The office is working with the Seventh Precinct, and the Parks Department reports on needle collection each week. Action: Ask the Seventh Precinct and the Parks Department for a status update on the Seward Park drug activity, and ask DOT and Parks to fix or report out-of-service lights in the dark areas, with 311 reports as the first step.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP community market terms
tickets.summary: The Land Use and Economic Development subcommittees met jointly on the EDC request for proposals for Essex Market, but EDC could not say how the board's two resolutions were reflected in the RFP. The board asked EDC to postpone issuing the RFP so that the terms keep the market community-oriented. Action: Hold the scheduled meeting with EDC this week, confirm whether the resolutions were incorporated, and push for the RFP issuance to be postponed.

tickets.title: SLA denial recommendation for 11 Allen Street
tickets.summary: The board voted 20 to 10 with nine abstentions to recommend denial of a full liquor license for 11 Allen Street, the operator's new location, which is near a saturated area and the former Time Cafe location with its crowd problems. Because the SLA can approve a license without the board's stipulations if no one appears, the board's denial needs community members and elected official support at the SLA hearing. Action: Have the community board office organize residents to attend the SLA hearing, and add the 311 complaint history and crowd evidence to the resolution.

tickets.title: Public restrooms pilot at Delancey Plaza
tickets.requester: Mayor's office representative (Oie); Transportation committee chair (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The city began installing 17 free public restrooms citywide in a one-year pilot, with one planned near Delancey Plaza and another at Cooper Square and East Sixth Street. The board has concerns about access rules, who uses the restrooms, and emergency calls, and a resolution is planned for next month. Action: Vote on the transportation committee resolution next month, and ask DOT to address the access and emergency-call concerns and to help identify good locations and partners.

tickets.title: Mobile voting option for CEC elections
tickets.requester: Health and Human Services committee (unnamed presenter); former CEC president (public speaker)
tickets.summary: CEC parent elections have turnout near 2 percent, partly because many households only have a smartphone and some parents are not signed into the NYC Schools account. The resolution asks for a mobile-first pilot that keeps in-person voting, with multilingual outreach, and clear messaging that immigration status is not asked or collected. Action: Vote on the resolution urging NYC public schools and the Office of Family and Community Empowerment to pilot a mobile voting option and expand parent outreach.

tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot proposal
tickets.summary: A public speaker who modeled MTA trip data says the Third Avenue L stop is little used, with only about 5 percent of riders getting on or off, and that closing it would save riders about 1,800 hours each day. The speaker says the stop is not a transfer station and is not wheelchair accessible. Action: Refer the proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot closure of the Third Avenue L stop.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exits and Canal Street redesign update
tickets.requester: Arnett (Transportation committee member); transportation committee chair
tickets.summary: The board sent a letter to the mayor and DOT restating its concerns about the Manhattan Bridge exits, citing a recent fatal crash, and asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project, which has had no update since January. Action: Follow up with DOT and the mayor's office for a written response to the letter and an update on the Canal Street redesign.

tickets.title: Bylaws attendance procedure revisions
tickets.requester: Diane (board member, bylaws committee); board member (unnamed)
tickets.summary: The proposed bylaws change would replace removal for missed meetings with a notice and meeting with the executive committee after the first problem, limit removal to a second issue, and require public members to follow conflict-of-interest rules. A question was raised about the double recommendation step. Action: Vote on the proposed bylaws at the October full board, with the 28-day notice emailed to members in advance, and clarify who makes the removal recommendation.

tickets.title: Congestion pricing effect on FDR traffic
tickets.summary: A member asked whether congestion pricing increased traffic on the FDR, since the MTA and DOT air quality report projected possible congestion there and the board had passed a resolution on it. The chair said this was not on the committee's list. Action: Ask MTA or DOT to report on actual FDR congestion after congestion pricing, and request any planned reporting.
